topic.title: Effects of urban green space on adolescent mental health
alternatives: Neighbourhood greenness and depressive symptoms in adolescents

research_question: Is exposure to urban green space associated with fewer depressive and anxiety symptoms in adolescents, and through which pathways?
project_context: Master's thesis using a regional school-based survey linked to satellite-derived greenness (NDVI).

streams.name: Green space exposure assessment
streams.description: NDVI, land-use data, park access, residential vs activity-space exposure.

streams.name: Adolescent mental health outcomes
streams.description: Depression, anxiety, wellbeing scales validated for adolescents.

streams.name: Mechanisms and pathways
streams.description: Physical activity, social cohesion, stress reduction, air pollution and noise mitigation.

streams.name: Methods and confounding
streams.description: Cohort vs cross-sectional designs, socioeconomic confounding, spatial analysis, multilevel models.

openalex_filters.note: 2739 = Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health; 2738 = Psychiatry and Mental health. Filled in by setup via https://api.openalex.org/subfields?search=<discipline>.

relevance_rubric.9-10: Quantitative study linking green-space exposure to adolescent mental-health outcomes with adequate confounder control.
relevance_rubric.7-8: Strong evidence on one stream that transfers (e.g., adult green-space studies with rigorous exposure assessment; validated adolescent outcome measures).
relevance_rubric.5-6: Adjacent context: theory, reviews, or other age groups or exposures.
